peer_protocol_review.scope: Independent todo_acceptance source check of existing server LIMIT/status/lexer/SQL semantics; accepted scoped with quote-cursor fixture correction pending at the earlier draft.

findings.finding: All public graph-query pages enumerate exact source paths and byte sizes. Same-count wrong identity, unexpected paths, mismatched bytes and duplicate expected paths reject. Missing admitted paths remain Unknown. Only the single exact generated root .codecortex.json is explicitly recorded and excluded from admitted source, never arbitrary hidden files.

findings.topic: finite keyset pagination and cursor integrity
findings.finding: Each page requires row_count==actual length, limit_applied64, truncatedfalse and at most64; canonical relative paths and strictly ascending cursor order reject malformed/duplicate/non-progress responses. Observed entries may not exceed initial indexed_count or source-count+one control bound; a short/empty final page terminates. No count-only success or unbounded OFFSET scan is introduced.

Before/after status must have equal index_epoch and indexed counts equal the complete observed inventory. This establishes the declared paths/sizes observation; it does not itself claim content-hash equality, which remains the separate source/manifest lock responsibility.

Cursor quotes are escaped for the existing lexer/parameterized SQL protocol; forbidden backslashes/non-relative paths reject; adapter enforces the existing4096-byte query limit before server sanitization.

The adapter preserves before status and each successful received page before validation, adds after/inventory observations before the final check, and runner writes readiness-observation after readiness returns an error. It does not manufacture unavailable failed-transport payloads.

Current real test quotes both i62 and i63, covering presence/absence of the generated first control row, and explicitly asserts an actual observed page query contains the escaped quote. All original137-file,3-page and exact-path/byte checks remain. The same-count wrong-path negative still uses real files and real MCP and expects a protocol failure.

Five unit controls cover wrong paths, missing/control, size/count/epoch, malformed/duplicate/order/relative pages, and quote/query limit; two real subprocess controls remain ignored unless an explicit built binary and --ignored are provided. A green zero-selected-tests run cannot satisfy them.
